lifting gas: A gas, such as helium or hydrogen, that is used to produce buoyancy for e.g. balloons or airships.
lifting shop: A workshop where vehicles are lifted off their bogies for maintenance work to be carried out.
lifting span: A span of a bridge that can be raised to allow boats and ships through; these can have different forms.
liftman: A person employed to operate a lift.
liftoff: The point in the launch of a rocket or an aircraft where it leaves contact with the ground.
The point at which a person or animal leaves the ground, as for example when jumping.
The point of launching into success or action.
ligand field theory: A theory, a combination of the earlier crystal field theory with molecular orbital theory, that describes the structure of coordination compounds.
ligase: Any of a group of enzymes that catalyze the binding of two molecules; synthetase.
ligate: To bind with a ligature or bandage.
To connect text characters with a ligature.
ligation: The act of tying, of applying a ligature.
The state of having a ligature, of being tied.
The act of tying off or sealing a blood vessel, fallopian tube, etc during surgery; act of ligating.
liger: An animal born to a male lion and a tigress.
light a fire under: To motivate or encourage (someone) to start sooner or move faster.
light air: A light wind with wind speed between 0.3 and 1.5 m/s; a Force 1 wind strength on the Beaufort scale.
light along: To lift or carry anything along the deck; to help in hauling along.
light art: A visual art form where physical light is the main or sole medium of creation.
light at the end of the tunnel: A better situation after long hardship.
A vision of a bright light, surrounded by darkness, seen by a dying person
light blue: A pale blue colour: sky blue or similar.
A member of the Cambridge rowing team.
light breeze: On the Beaufort scale, a force-2 wind (4-6 knots)
light bulb joke: Any joke of the form "How many X does it take to change a light bulb?" followed by a witty riposte, where X is some usually stereotypical class of people.
light buoy: A buoy with a light on top which is lit at night to aid navigation.
light carrier: A category of aircraft carrier smaller in size and with a lower aircraft complement than a navy's standard carriers.
light cavalry: A military unit consisting of lightly armed and lightly armored troops mounted on horses.
light chain: The small polypeptide subunit of a protein complex.
light cone: In special relativity, the pattern describing the temporal evolution of a flash of light in Minkowski spacetime. This is modeled in 3-space using the two horizontal axes as spatial dimensions, while the vertical axis is time.
A (realized or imagined) data visualization of possible sets of future outcomes that is analogous to such a cone.
light cream: Pasteurized cream at least 18 percent of which, but less than 30% of which, is milkfat, optionally homogenized, and optionally containing added flavor, nutritive sweetener, emulsifier, or stabilizer.
A cream at least 18 percent of which is fat.
light cruiser: A type of cruiser, defined in the 1930 London Naval Treaty as having a main gun battery of 6.1-inch caliber (155mm) or smaller.
light curve: a graph of the intensity of radiation from an astronomical object as it changes with time
light day: A unit of length equal to the distance light travels in one day; about 170 astronomical units
light decade: A unit of length equal to the distance light travels in one decade.
light due: A duty or toll levied on ships navigating certain waters, for the maintenance of lighthouses; light money.
light echo: A phenomenon caused by light reflected off surfaces distant from the source, and arriving at the observer with a delay relative to this distance, analogous to an echo of sound.
light elf: One of a race of elves who live above ground and are radiant.
A member of the race of Ljósalfar, daylight dwelling elves or nature spirits (as opposed to the underground dwelling dark elves or dwarves).
light engine: A locomotive running on its own, or with other powered locomotives, with no wagons or carriages attached.
light entertainment: Radio and television programming that includes comedies, variety shows, game shows, quiz shows, etc.
light fantastic: A dance or the act of dancing.
light field: A function of all the light flowing through all points of space in a particular volume
light fixture: A complete lighting unit, composed of a housing attached to a wall or ceiling, and a mount for a light source.
light gun: A device resembling a gun that allows the player of a video game to target a point on the screen.
light hour: A unit of length equal to the distance light travels in one hour
light industry: Any industry that does not require high capitalization or heavy machinery.
light infantry: Ground combat soldiers who are not mechanized, and whose role is to harass the enemy in front of the main body of infantry.
light intensity: The amount of light emitted by a light source per unit of time.
light line: The waterline at which a vessel floats when at light displacement; the light waterline.
light machine gun: A lightweight machine gun designed to be operated by a single person; such guns use rifle cartridges, whereas submachine guns use pistol cartridges.
light matter: Any form of matter that is not dark matter.
light meter: Any of various devices that measure some property of light
light microscope: A scientific instrument which provides a magnified view of very small objects that are illuminated with visible light which then passes through optical lenses.
light minute: A unit of length equal to the distance light travels in one minute.
light money: Money levied for the maintenance of lighthouses; light dues.
light novel: A Japanese novel primarily targeting young adults, typically illustrated (in an anime/manga style) and containing not more than 50,000 words.
light off: To light the fire on a gas boiler to turn it on.
To ignite properly and begin functioning.
light oil: Any of various types of low-viscosity lubricating oil. Sometimes named for principal uses (e.g., spindle oil, sewing machine oil).
The oily product, lighter than water, forming the chief fraction of the first distillate of coal tar, and consisting largely of benzene and toluene.
light on: To find or think of something unexpectedly; to come upon something by accident.
light on the hill: Used to evoke the values of the Australian Labor Party.
light opera: A sung dramatic work of a light or comic nature, usually with a happy ending and often including spoken dialogue.
light out: To go away or depart, especially in haste or without notice.
light painting: The artistic technique of moving a light source to selectively illuminate parts of the subject or scene a camera is recording (at a slow shutter speed), or to shine directly into the camera and in this way sketch.

Camera painting, the artistic technique of moving a camera (while it records at a low shutter speed) such that light sources appear in multiple places or as streaks in the resulting photograph, the "painting".
A painting created using one of these techniques.
light paper: A short white paper; a brief factual report detailing a new product or technology.
light pen: A pen-like device allowing a computer user to interact with the screen display.
light pollution: An excess of artificial light, especially near urban areas, reducing visibility of stars, etc. in the night sky.
light rail: A kind of passenger railway in urban and suburban settings typically characterized by a mixture of tram (or in North America streetcar) and metro features, crossing streets at grade crossings and normally powered by electricity.
light rail system: A kind of passenger railway in urban and suburban settings typically characterized by a mixture of tram (or in North America streetcar) and metro features, crossing streets at grade crossings and normally powered by electricity.
